title: Unix datagram SCM_RIGHTS references can form ownership cycles
mechanism: UnixDatagramSocket -> MessageReceiver -> Arc<MessageQueue> -> Message -> AuxiliaryData files -> Arc<UnixDatagramSocket> forms a strong cycle when a datagram socket is sent into its own queue. AuxiliaryData::from_control checks only UnixStreamSocket, and no collector exists, so MessageReceiver::drop never runs.
contract: Unreachable Unix sockets kept alive only by in-flight SCM_RIGHTS references are reclaimed by the Unix garbage collector (Linux net/unix/garbage.c).
observed: Source only: a datagram socket sent into its own queue keeps itself alive after all descriptors close, so its queue, carried files and bound address are never released.

repro.how_to_run: No reproducer. finding.md Reproduction describes a self-SCM_RIGHTS send on an abstract-bound datagram socket followed by close and a rebind of the same name.

caveats: Ownership graph source-confirmed, runtime release consequence untested. #2176 discusses the stream-socket hazard, and the datagram/self-FD instance is a scope extension. Report T-9 is AST-34 but brief T-9 is AST-35.
